Longitudinal Summary

Over the period from Q1 2021 through Q4 2023, Tesla's net income attributable to common stockholders showed a strong upward trajectory, growing from $438 million in Q1 2021 to $15.00 billion for the full year 2023. The company consistently reported favorable changes in net income compared to prior periods, driven primarily by increases in net income excluding non-cash expenses, gains, and losses, partially offset at times by changes in net operating assets and liabilities. Notably, in 2021 and 2022, Tesla recorded full valuation allowances on its U.S. deferred tax assets, which were later released in 2023, resulting in a significant one-time non-cash benefit of $5.9 billion. Management highlighted record production, deliveries, and profitability milestones throughout the periods, culminating in accumulated profitability turning positive in 2021 and substantial net income growth thereafter.

Forecasting Credibility: None

No guidance versus actual pairs for net income were provided in the evidence, so it is not possible to assess management's forecasting credibility for this topic. Without forward guidance figures paired with actual results, no pattern of met, exceeded, or missed expectations can be established. Therefore, the forecasting credibility rating must remain null.

Trends

  • Strong net income growth over time
  • Increasing net income excluding non-cash items
  • Fluctuations in net operating assets and liabilities impacting net income
  • Full valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets in 2021 and 2022
  • Release of valuation allowance in 2023 causing one-time income boost

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • Impact of non-cash expenses, gains, and losses on net income
  • Changes in net operating assets and liabilities affecting reported net income
  • Deferred tax asset valuation allowances and their reversals

Key Concerns

  • The presence of a full valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets in 2021 and 2022, followed by its release in 2023, introduces significant non-recurring impacts on net income that complicate trend analysis.
  • No forward guidance on net income was provided, limiting the ability to evaluate management's forecasting accuracy for this key metric.

Conclusion

Tesla's net income attributable to common stockholders has demonstrated robust growth from 2021 through 2023, with reported figures rising from $438 million in Q1 2021 to $15.00 billion for the full year 2023. This growth was driven largely by operational improvements reflected in net income excluding non-cash items, though it was occasionally offset by changes in net operating assets and liabilities. The accounting treatment of deferred tax assets, including a full valuation allowance in 2021 and 2022 and a substantial release in 2023, materially affected net income figures, contributing a one-time non-cash benefit of $5.9 billion in 2023. Despite the absence of forward guidance on net income, the consistent upward trend and management commentary on record profitability milestones indicate strong financial performance over the period.

  • jump to section"11 Net Income per Share of Common Stock Attributable to Common Stockholders Basic net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders is calculated by dividing net income attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average shares of common stock outstanding for the period."
  • jump to section"During the three months ended March 31, 2021 , we increased net income attributable to common stockholders by $ 5 million to arrive at the numerator used to calculate diluted net income per share, which represents the interest expense recognized on the convertible debt instruments that were subject to this change in methodology."
  • jump to section"This had the effect of increasing our basic and diluted net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders for the three months ended March 31, 2021 by $ 0.15 and $ 0.13 , respectively."
  • jump to section"The change in methodology to determine the denominator used in the calculation of diluted net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders contributed less than $ 0.01 of the increase by requiring the use of the if-converted method as discussed above."
  • jump to section"The following table presents the reconciliation of basic to diluted weighted average shares used in computing net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders, as adjusted to give effect to the five-for-one stock split effected in the form of a stock dividend in August 2020 (the “Stock Split”) (in millions): Three Months Ended March 31, 2021 2020 Weighted average shares used in computing net income per share of common stock, basic 961 915 Add: Stock-based awards 97 46 Convertible senior notes (1) 21 30 Warrants 54 3 Weighted average shares used in computing net income per share of common stock, diluted 1,133 994 The following table presents the potentially dilutive shares that were excluded from the computation of diluted net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders, because their effect was anti-dilutive, as adjusted to give effect to the Stock Split (in millions): Three Months Ended March 31, 2021 2020 Stock-based awards 0 0 Convertible senior notes (1) 1 2 (1) Under the modified retrospective method of adoption of ASU 2020-06, the dilutive impact of convertible senior notes was calculated using the if-converted method for the three months ended March 31, 2021."
  • jump to section"Such gains are presented net of impairment losses in Restructuring and other in the consolidated statement of operations."
  • jump to section"Accordingly, our interest rate swaps are recorded at fair value on the consolidated balance sheets within Other non-current assets or Other long-term liabilities, with any changes in their fair values recognized as Other income (expense), net, in the consolidated statements of operations and with any cash flows recognized as operating activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows."
  • jump to section"We write-down inventory for any excess or obsolete inventories or when we believe that the net realizable value of inventories is less than the carrying value."
  • jump to section"This results in us recording the cost of their production equipment within Property, plant and equipment, net, on the consolidated balance sheets with a corresponding liability recorded to debt and finance leases."
  • jump to section"The proceeds from the issuance, net of discounts and fees, were $ 1.07 billion."
  • jump to section"As we now expect to settle a portion of the 2024 Notes in the second quarter of 2021, we reclassified $ 51 million of the carrying value of the 2024 Notes from debt and finance leases, net of current portion to current portion of debt and finance leases on our consolidated balance sheet as of March 31, 2021."
  • jump to section"The differences between the unpaid principal balances and the net carrying values are due to debt discounts or deferred financing costs."
  • jump to section"Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders before interest expense, provision (benefit) for income taxes, depreciation and amortization and stock-based compensation."
  • jump to section"Cash distributions of income and other receipts by a fund, net of agreed upon expenses, estimated expenses, tax benefits and detriments of income and loss and tax credits, are allocated to the fund investor and our subsidiary as specified in the agreements."

MD&A
  • jump to section"During the three and six months ended June 30, 2021, our net income attributable to common stockholders was $1.14 billion and $1.58 billion, respectively, representing favorable changes of $1.04 billion and $1.46 billion, respectively, over the same periods ended June 30, 2020."
  • jump to section"Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests and redeemable noncontrolling interests increased by $11 million, or 44%, in the three months ended June 30, 2021 as compared to the three months ended June 30, 2020."
  • jump to section"Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests and redeemable noncontrolling interests decreased by $15 million, or 19%, in the six months ended June 30, 2021 as compared to the six months ended June 30, 2020."
  • jump to section"This increase was primarily due to the increase in net income excluding non-cash expenses and gains of $1.88 billion and the overall decrease in net operating assets and liabilities of $1.36 billion."
  • jump to section"Cash Flows from Financing Activities Net cash used in financing activities during the six months ended June 30, 2021 was $2.57 billion, which consisted primarily of $1.95 billion of cash repayments upon conversions of our convertible senior notes, $614 million of repayments under our Fixed Asset Facility, $294 million of repayments under our 2016 Warehouse Agreement, $151 million repayment of Solar Term Loan upon maturity and $196 million principal repayments of our finance leases."

  • jump to section"12 Net Income per Share of Common Stock Attributable to Common Stockholders Basic net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders is calculated by dividing net income attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average shares of common stock outstanding for the period."
  • jump to section"During the three and six months ended June 30, 2021 , we increased net income attributable to common stockholders by $ 2 million and $ 6 million, respectively, to arrive at the numerator used to calculate diluted net income per share, which represents the interest expense recognized on the convertible debt instruments that were subject to this change in methodology."
  • jump to section"This had the effect of increasing our basic and diluted net income per share of common stock attributable to common stockholders by $ 0.05 and $ 0.04 , respectively, for the three months ended June 30, 2021 and by $ 0.20 and $ 0.18 , respectively, for the six months ended June 30, 2021 ."
